subject: Re: StarLedger security questionnaire — data jurisdiction & retention
messages:
From: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@starledger.com>

Cc: DPO Team <dpo@starledger.com>

Subject: Data residency / retention questions (StarLedger security questionnaire)

Neha —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Attached is the security questionnaire our legal & DPO teams put together for hosted API customers. We have a couple of high-priority questions we need clarified before we move forward with procurement:

1) Data residency: for the hosted API, can you guarantee that user-content (requests and model outputs) will remain in the EU region (Frankfurt/Amsterdam) at-rest and in transit? If not guaranteed, what are the typical data flow patterns and what controls do we have?

2) Retention windows: what default retention windows do you apply to request payloads, embeddings, and logs (request/response bodies, trace logs, audit logs)? Are there separate TTLs for customer-managed keys vs. Redwood-managed keys?

3) Deletion / erasure: if StarLedger makes a written erasure request, what is the process and SLA for removing data from active stores, caches, and backups? Do you provide a verifiable deletion statement?

4) Backups & snapshots: how long are backups retained, where are they stored geographically, and are they included in erasure requests?

5) Encryption & access: please confirm encryption at-rest and in-transit; who has access to raw request/response content for support or debugging (Redwood staff, contractors, or third-party vendors)?

We appreciate concise, point-by-point answers we can include with our vendor risk assessment.

Best,
Miguel
Miguel Santos
Lead Security Architect — StarLedger Health

Subject: Re: Data residency / retention questions (StarLedger security questionnaire)

Hi Miguel —

Thanks for sending this along and for the clear list. Below are concise, customer-ready answers for each item; I’ve called out where contractual addenda (DPA / security appendix) are recommended. If you’d like, we can also supply a short one-page statement for your vendor review pack.

1) Data residency
- Hosted API regioning: By default requests are routed to the nearest Redwood region to minimize latency. For customers requiring EU-only processing we offer a geo-restriction option on hosted accounts that pins inference and short-term storage to our EU region (currently Amsterdam and Frankfurt).
- Guarantee level: When the geo-restriction option is enabled we commit (via the security appendix) to process and store request/response content only within the specified region for the active retention window. Metadata required for billing and routing (minimal routing tags) may be processed outside region for control plane functions but are pseudonymized and aggregated.

2) Retention windows
- Request/response payloads (hosted API): default TTL is 30 days. This covers active telemetry and short-term debugging caches.
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: by default we persist embeddings for 90 days to support similarity features; customers can opt-out or request shorter TTLs.
- Operational logs / traces: short-lived traces are retained for 7 days; higher-fidelity audit logs are retained for 365 days (used for security/audit purposes).
- Key management: if you use Redwood-managed encryption keys, the above TTLs apply. For customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) we can provide options to reduce retention of decrypted artifacts; note that some operational metadata may remain to meet billing/SLA obligations.

3) Deletion / erasure process
- Process: StarLedger submits an erasure request to privacy@redwood.com and to your account rep. We run a multi-stage purge: (a) remove from active stores and caches within 72 hours (b) mark records for deletion in secondary stores; (c) remove references in search/indexing within 7 days.
- Backups: deletions from backups follow our backup rotation policy (see backups below). Backups are encrypted; we will isolate affected backup segments and ensure no restores occur for the purged data.
- Verification: after deletion we provide a deletion confirmation letter that includes scope, timestamps, and the systems impacted. This is included in our DPA as an optional deliverable.

4) Backups & snapshots
- Retention: periodic backups and snapshots are retained for up to 90 days in the EU region for disaster recovery.
- Geography: backups for EU-geofenced accounts are stored in the EU region only.
- Inclusion in erasure: we flag and exclude purged data from future restores; because of snapshot mechanics there may be a short window where data exists in immutable backup segments — we will isolate and remediate those segments and confirm mitigation in our deletion certificate.

5) Encryption & access
- Encryption: all data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we use AES-256. Customer-managed KMS integrates with our encryption layer for keys.
- Access controls: only a small, audited set of Redwood SRE/support engineers have the ability to access raw request/response content for troubleshooting. Access is time-limited, logged, and requires a ticket with justification. Contractors are allowed only via vetted vendor agreements and are not granted access to production data by default.

Attachments I’m including: a short one-pager summary (redwood_data-handling-summary-2028-11.pdf) and a suggested language snippet for a DPA/addendum on geo-restriction and deletion SLA.

If that covers things for now I’ll loop in Legal to draft the DPA appendix and send your DPO a verification template.

Thanks —

Neha —

Thanks for the fast reply. A couple of follow-ups from our DPO:

• Backups: when you say "isolate and remediate those segments" — can you confirm whether you will (a) re-encrypt and rotate the backup set to remove access paths, (b) or perform a targeted purge of the segments containing the data? Our security team prefers targeted eradication when feasible.

• Verification: can the deletion confirmation include cryptographic evidence (hashes/timestamps) or is it an administrative statement only?

• Support access: please confirm the escalation path when a support engineer needs to access request/response content for a live incident. We need a 4-eyes approval and a logged ticket in a system we can audit.

Also, please share the SOC 2 report redacted summary and the DPA language you mentioned.

Best,
Miguel

Miguel —

Appreciate the follow-ups — answers below and next steps at the end.

• Backups: our primary remediation path for geofenced accounts is targeted: we identify affected backup segments and perform a targeted purge where possible, then re-key remaining backups and rotate snapshots to remove any remaining logical access. If regulatory constraints prevent targeted purges we will isolate the impacted snapshots and apply mitigations, documented in the deletion confirmation. We’ll confirm the exact approach in the DPA appendix to meet StarLedger’s preference for targeted eradication when possible.

• Verification evidence: we provide a deletion certificate that includes scoped hashes and system timestamps where feasible (hashes of object identifiers rather than raw content). For additional assurance we can include signed timestamps from our internal archival system. We can discuss the exact cryptographic artifacts your DPO prefers during the legal review.

• Support access / escalation: our policy requires a support ticket opened in our tracking system with business justification, two-person approval (SRE manager + security reviewer), and an entry in the audit log. We can provide your DPO read-only access to the audit entries related to your account upon request or deliver a periodic access log export (CSV) covering specific incidents.

Attachments / links:
- SOC 2 summary (redacted) can be shared under NDA; I’ve looped Laura (Legal) to propose the disclosure flow.
- DPA appendix language and a sample deletion certificate template are attached in the redwood_data-handling-summary-2028-11.pdf we already included.

Next steps:
1) I’ll ask Legal to draft a short geo-restriction + deletion SLA appendix for the DPA and circulate it for review (target: 5 business days).
2) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical session (Karthik + SRE) to walk your DPO through the backup mechanics and verification artifacts.

Happy to set up the call — what times work for your team next week?
